project.name: mdbtools
project.commit_note: The exact staged vulnerable checkout in `gt_results/arvo_30752/_work/src/mdbtools` matches metadata vulnerable commit `0e3a627ee6b3828b8dde3a0c105bf73454c45959`. The staged `patch.diff` is its direct child `89e23615828ea64af9858e5942d6bc4d82c458a6` and changes only `src/libmdb/iconv.c`, replacing `while (1)` with `while (len_out)` in `decompressed_to_utf8_with_iconv()`.

classification.classification_note: The saved Stage 01 symptom is a later wild-pointer read in `mdb_xfer_bound_data()`, but the rebuilt source trace and the direct-child fix commit ground the underlying bug in `decompressed_to_utf8_with_iconv()`: once its output budget is exhausted, the `'?'` fallback can write past a 16 KB heap buffer and corrupt later heap state.

analysis_state.reason: The trace is now re-anchored at `mdb_open_buffer()`'s `fmemopen(buffer, len, ...)` source and threads the fuzz-backed stream through `_mdb_read_pg()`, page-0 JET3/code-page parsing, JET3 iconv initialization, catalog bind-buffer installation, earlier row-field materialization, and the earlier bound-text conversion path. The causal chain is closed at the actual corrupting write in `decompressed_to_utf8_with_iconv()`: after `len_out` reaches zero, the unconditional loop can still take the invalid-input fallback, `*out_ptr++ = '?'` writes past the 16 KB temporary `text` buffer, and `len_out--` wraps. A later null-field bind then reuses one corrupted `col->bind_ptr` in `strcpy(col->bind_ptr, "")`, matching the saved ASan sink. Stage 01 still does not preserve which adjacent heap object was overwritten or which later bound column carried the bad pointer, but the source-level corruption-to-sink chain is explicit and consistent with the staged patch.

bug_description.original_source: sample_info.json.issue_description / exact staged vulnerable source / patch.diff / sanitizer_trace.txt / vulnerable_compile.log
bug_description.normalized: Stage 01 reproduced `AddressSanitizer: SEGV on unknown address` at `strcpy(col->bind_ptr, "")` in `src/libmdb/data.c:270` with stack `mdb_xfer_bound_data -> _mdb_attempt_bind -> mdb_read_row -> mdb_fetch_row -> mdb_read_catalog`. In the exact staged vulnerable source, the 4122-byte witness is first wrapped by `mdb_open_buffer()` as an in-memory stream, and later `_mdb_read_pg()` reads page 0 from that same stream into `mdb->pg_buf`. Page-0 byte `0x14` is `0x00`, so the handle selects JET3, and page-0 bytes `0x3c-0x3d` are `0x0000`, so `mdb_iconv_init()` falls through its JET3 default case and installs `mdb->iconv_in/out` for CP1252-backed `iconv` conversion. `mdb_read_catalog()` then allocates five 16 KB bind buffers, stores them into the bound `MSysObjects` columns' `MdbColumn.bind_ptr` fields, and iterates catalog rows. On an earlier bound non-null text-field iteration during that same catalog walk, `mdb_read_row()` forwards attacker-derived `fields[i].start` and `fields[i].siz` into `_mdb_attempt_bind()`, `mdb_xfer_bound_data()` calls `mdb_col_to_string()`, and `mdb_col_to_string()` allocates a 16 KB temporary `text` buffer before calling `mdb_unicode2ascii()`. Because this vulnerable build has iconv enabled, `mdb_unicode2ascii()` dispatches to `decompressed_to_utf8_with_iconv()`, whose unconditional `while (1)` loop can keep taking the invalid-input fallback after `len_out` has reached zero. At that point `*out_ptr++ = '?'` writes past the end of the temporary `text` buffer and `len_out--` wraps to a huge value, corrupting adjacent heap state. Later in the same catalog walk, another bound non-boolean column is parsed as null, so `_mdb_attempt_bind()` takes `mdb_xfer_bound_data(mdb, 0, col, 0)`. That null fast path reuses the now-corrupted `col->bind_ptr`, and `strcpy(col->bind_ptr, "")` dereferences the wild pointer reported by ASan. The exact overwritten heap object and exact later column identity are not preserved in Stage 01, but the direct-child patch fixes this earlier overflow by changing `while (1)` to `while (len_out)`.

source.description: Earliest project-side materialization of the attacker buffer into the stream object later used by every MDB page read on both the overflow and crash paths.
source.value_from: The exact staged 4122-byte `poc` is passed as `buffer,len` to `mdb_open_buffer()`. This statement wraps those bytes with `fmemopen()`, so later `_mdb_read_pg()` calls read page 0, table pages, and catalog data pages directly from the witness.

root_cause.description: Out-of-bounds fallback write after the 16 KB conversion buffer is exhausted. Because the loop keeps running with `len_out == 0`, this statement writes past the end of the temporary `text` buffer and the following `len_out--` wraps the remaining-length counter.
root_cause.note: The direct-child patch changes the loop guard at line 54 from `while (1)` to `while (len_out)`, which prevents this exhausted-output iteration entirely. Stage 01 does not preserve which adjacent heap object is overwritten, only the later corrupted `col->bind_ptr` manifestation.

sink.description: Saved AddressSanitizer crash site. The later null-field bind reuses a corrupted bound pointer and dereferences it while trying to write an empty string.
sink.note: The saved sanitizer trace reports `AddressSanitizer: SEGV on unknown address` caused by a READ at this line with stack `mdb_xfer_bound_data -> _mdb_attempt_bind -> mdb_read_row`.

tainted_value_origin.description: The row parser turns current-row bytes into per-column null bits and byte-slice metadata. Earlier non-null iterations feed text conversion into the iconv helper, and the later crashing iteration feeds the null-field bind.

parser_admitted.description: The staged witness is admitted far enough as an MDB file that `mdb_read_catalog()` iterates `MSysObjects` rows. That same catalog walk covers the earlier bound-text conversion and the later null-field crash.

coarse_trace.summary: The fuzz buffer is wrapped as an in-memory stream, page 0 is read from it, byte `0x14` selects JET3, bytes `0x3c-0x3d` set code page 0, and JET3 iconv conversion is initialized through the CP1252 default case.
Catalog setup allocates five 16 KB destination buffers for `MSysObjects`, stores them in bound `MdbColumn.bind_ptr` fields, and begins iterating catalog rows read from the fuzz-backed stream.

On an earlier bound non-null text-field iteration, row bytes are parsed into a slice, forwarded into text conversion, and the iconv helper overruns the temporary 16 KB `text` buffer once `len_out` is exhausted but invalid input remains.

Later in the same catalog walk, another bound non-boolean field is parsed as null, so `_mdb_attempt_bind()` takes `mdb_xfer_bound_data(mdb, 0, col, 0)` and reuses the corrupted bound-pointer state instead of building a fresh string.
The null-field fast path enters `if (!len)` and `strcpy(col->bind_ptr, "")` dereferences the wild pointer reported by ASan.

fine_trace.note: Source. The fuzzer-supplied `buffer,len` from the exact staged 4122-byte `poc` is wrapped as an in-memory `FILE*`. Every later `_mdb_read_pg()` call on both the overflow and crash paths reads MDB pages from this stream.
Page-0 materialization. `mdb_handle_from_stream()` immediately calls `mdb_read_pg(mdb, 0)`, and this `fread` copies page 0 from the fuzz-backed stream into `mdb->pg_buf`.
Page-0 byte `0x14` is read as `jet_version`. In the staged `poc`, byte `0x14` is `0x00`, so the handle stays on the JET3 format path.
Page-0 bytes `0x3c-0x3d` are read as the JET3 code page. In the staged `poc` those two bytes are `00 00`, so this field becomes `0`.

Because step 3 selected JET3 and step 4 produced code page `0`, `mdb_iconv_init()` falls through the default arm to `jet3_iconv_code = "CP1252"` and installs `mdb->iconv_in/out`. The staged vulnerable compile log records `checking for iconv... yes`, so later text conversion uses this iconv helper path rather than the no-iconv fallback.
Before iterating `MSysObjects`, `mdb_read_catalog()` allocates five 16 KB destination buffers sized by `mdb->bind_size`.

The subsequent `mdb_bind_column_by_name()` calls from `mdb_read_catalog()` store those heap buffers into the bound catalog columns' `col->bind_ptr` fields. These are the original valid destinations later corrupted/reused; one of the bound calls is for the string `Name` column.

During `mdb_fetch_row(table)` inside `mdb_read_catalog()`, later `_mdb_read_pg()` calls read catalog data pages from the same fuzz-backed stream into `mdb->pg_buf`. Those page bytes are the row data parsed on both the earlier overflow iteration and the later crashing null iteration.
Earlier on a bound non-null text-field iteration, the row parser decodes the null bitmap and sets `fields[i].is_null = 0`, so `_mdb_attempt_bind()` does not take the null fast path.

On that same earlier non-null text iteration, `mdb_crack_row()` materializes the field's byte offset and length inside the current row. Those attacker-derived bounds are the slice later forwarded into text conversion.
Still on that earlier bound text-column iteration, `mdb_read_row()` forwards the parsed null bit and byte slice into `_mdb_attempt_bind()`.

Because the earlier field is non-boolean and not null, `_mdb_attempt_bind()` takes the normal data-transfer arm and calls `mdb_xfer_bound_data()` with the attacker-derived `offset,len` instead of the null fast path.

fine_trace.code: str = mdb_col_to_string(mdb, mdb->pg_buf, start, col->col_type, len);
fine_trace.note: On that earlier text-bearing iteration, `mdb_xfer_bound_data()` asks `mdb_col_to_string()` to decode the field bytes into a temporary string.

For `MDB_TEXT`, `mdb_col_to_string()` allocates a fresh 16 KB heap buffer `text` and passes the attacker-controlled field bytes plus length into `mdb_unicode2ascii()`. This temporary `text` allocation is the later overflow object.

fine_trace.code: dlen = decompressed_to_utf8_with_iconv(mdb, in_ptr, len_in, dest, dlen);
fine_trace.note: Because step 5 installed `mdb->iconv_in` and this vulnerable build has iconv enabled, `mdb_unicode2ascii()` routes the field into `decompressed_to_utf8_with_iconv()` instead of the non-iconv fallback.

Control bug. The conversion loop keeps iterating even after the 16 KB output budget is exhausted; it stops only for `!len_in` or `errno == E2BIG`, so remaining invalid input can still fall into the `'?'` recovery path with `len_out == 0`.

Root cause. On that exhausted-output recovery iteration, this writes one byte past step 14's 16 KB `text` buffer and then decrements `len_out` from `0` to `SIZE_MAX`, so further helper activity can continue past the allocation. Stage 01 does not preserve which adjacent heap object is clobbered, only the later corrupted bound-pointer effect.

Later on the crashing iteration, the row parser decodes a bound non-boolean field as null, so `fields[i].is_null = 1`. That is the only source-level condition that sends `_mdb_attempt_bind()` into the `mdb_xfer_bound_data(mdb, 0, col, 0)` path seen in the ASan stack.
On that later crashing iteration, `mdb_read_row()` forwards the null field into `_mdb_attempt_bind()`. One of step 7's bound `col->bind_ptr` fields now carries the overflowed heap state from step 17.

For that later non-boolean null field, `_mdb_attempt_bind()` chooses `mdb_xfer_bound_data(mdb, 0, col, 0)`. This path does not build a fresh conversion buffer; it reuses the current `col->bind_ptr` state.
Inside `mdb_xfer_bound_data()`, `len == 0` selects the empty-string arm rather than computing a fresh source string.

Sink. `strcpy` dereferences the corrupted bound pointer, and the saved AddressSanitizer trace reports `SEGV on unknown address` caused by a READ at this line with stack `mdb_xfer_bound_data -> _mdb_attempt_bind -> mdb_read_row`.

sanitizer_ground_truth.patch_resolves_note: The direct-child patch changes `decompressed_to_utf8_with_iconv()` from `while (1)` to `while (len_out)`, which blocks the exhausted-output iteration that performs fine-trace step 17's out-of-bounds `'?'` write and the subsequent `len_out` wraparound. Stage 02 did not run the fixed image, so this remains source-level fix evidence rather than fixed-runtime confirmation.

cross_validation.root_cause_matches_allocation_context: ASan provides no allocation/free context for the late wild-pointer read. The direct-child patch nonetheless matches the earlier on-path source-level write that can corrupt later heap state: step 17's out-of-bounds fallback write in `decompressed_to_utf8_with_iconv()`.
cross_validation.trace_consistent_with_stack: Yes. The saved stack covers the later null-field portion of the chain at fine-trace steps 19-22 (`mdb_read_row -> _mdb_attempt_bind -> mdb_xfer_bound_data`) and the catalog-row checkpoint. Fine-trace steps 14-17 are the earlier source-grounded precursor corruption outside the crash stack.
cross_validation.tainted_value_reaches_sink: Yes. The fuzz-backed stream yields row bytes that `mdb_crack_row()` materializes into field state; an earlier bound text-field iteration routes attacker bytes through `mdb_unicode2ascii()` into the iconv overflow at step 17, and a later null-field iteration reuses the resulting corrupted `col->bind_ptr` at the `strcpy` sink.

poc.trigger: Stage 01's saved vulnerable run executed `PYTHONPATH=gt_generation python3 -m gt_toolkit arvo-workspace --result-dir /mnt/datastore/gt_generation/gt_results/arvo_30752 run --version vulnerable --expect crash`, which fed `poc` to `/out/fuzz_mdb` and reproduced `AddressSanitizer: SEGV on unknown address` in `mdb_xfer_bound_data`.

format.name: 4122-byte JET3 MDB witness with earlier iconv overflow and later null-field bind reuse
format.contract: The verified trigger semantics are limited to the exact staged 4122-byte `poc` in this result directory. The saved artifacts prove that `mdb_open_buffer()` wraps the witness as an in-memory stream, page-0 byte `0x14` is `0x00` so JET3 is selected, page-0 bytes `0x3c-0x3d` are `0x0000` so `mdb_iconv_init()` takes the JET3 default CP1252 iconv path, and `mdb_read_catalog()` binds 16 KB catalog buffers and iterates `MSysObjects` rows. Within that same catalog walk, an earlier bound non-null text-field conversion must reach `mdb_unicode2ascii()` and the vulnerable `decompressed_to_utf8_with_iconv()` helper with exhausted output space plus remaining invalid input, so step 17 writes past the 16 KB temporary `text` buffer. Later, a bound non-boolean field must be parsed as null so `_mdb_attempt_bind()` takes `mdb_xfer_bound_data(mdb, 0, col, 0)` and `strcpy(col->bind_ptr, "")` faults. The staged artifacts do not preserve which earlier row/column overflowed or which later bound column carried the corrupted pointer, so this contract should not be generalized beyond witnesses that recreate that same earlier-overflow / later-null-bind sequence.

evidence_limitations: The saved AddressSanitizer trace records only the late wild-pointer read at `src/libmdb/data.c:270`; it does not name the exact adjacent heap object overwritten by the earlier `src/libmdb/iconv.c` overflow or which specific later bound column reused the corrupted pointer.
Stage 01 preserved only vulnerable-build execution, so `patch_resolves` remains a source-level conclusion from the direct-child diff rather than fixed-runtime confirmation.

The fix commit message references OSS-Fuzz 28832+28807 rather than issue 30752, so the patch/sample linkage here rests on direct parent-child provenance plus the on-path `src/libmdb/iconv.c` change, not on matching public issue IDs.
